source: master session 2026-08-17 — NU software article publish

lessons.title: A Cloudflare Pages deploy from a non-production branch silently becomes a preview
lessons.problem: Deploying with `wrangler pages deploy` inherits the local git branch name. If the Pages project's production branch is `main` and the repo is on `master`, the deploy succeeds — as a preview. Production keeps serving the old build while every success message looks normal.
method: Before deploying, compare the local branch to the Pages project's production branch (project settings or latest_deployment.deployment_trigger.metadata.branch).
After deploy, verify the APEX domain — not the per-deploy preview URL — serves the new content.
signals_it_applies: Deploy output shows an alias URL named after a branch that is not the production branch
The preview URL has the change but the custom domain does not
hard_nos: Do not conclude propagation delay before checking which branch the deploy landed on
lessons.evidence: nothingunseen.com 2026-08-17: repo on master, production on main; first deploy aliased master.nothingunseen.pages.dev and apex stayed stale; redeploy with --branch main fixed it.

lessons.title: HTTP 200 on a Pages site proves nothing — SPA fallback answers 200 for missing pages
lessons.problem: Cloudflare Pages serves the fallback document for unknown paths with status 200, so a new page can look live while production is actually serving the homepage shell.
method: Verify by matching a distinctive string from the new page's body, never by status code.
Pair the content check with one functional check that exercises the new code path (e.g. the search API returning the new entry).
hard_nos: Do not report a page as live from a 200 alone
Do not skip the content match because the deploy command succeeded
lessons.evidence: nothingunseen.com 2026-08-17: /a/nu-cloudflare-ops-mcp-agent-harness returned 200 while production served the fallback; content-match check exposed it before it was reported as done.

lessons.title: A published article is page + index + sitemap + llms.txt + ping, not just an HTML file
lessons.problem: Dropping an HTML file on a site does not make it findable by search engines, site search, or AI crawlers.
method: Follow the site's own house template exactly (styles, disclosure footer, Reading Room link).
Register the piece in the site's search index with title, excerpt, tags, and image.
Add the URL to sitemap.xml and describe the subject in llms.txt for AI crawlers.
Add JSON-LD appropriate to the content (SoftwareApplication for a tool, NewsArticle for the piece).
Submit via IndexNow after the production deploy is verified, not before.
Disclose shared ownership when the site covers its own publisher's product.
lessons.evidence: nothingunseen.com 2026-08-17: article ranked first in NU search for its target query after full wiring; IndexNow accepted 191 URLs.
